newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa current account down sharply in Q3 - Stals.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa current account down sharply in Q3 - Stals.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday that South Africa's current account deficit, on an annualised basis, had fallen by six billion rand to 10 billion rand in the third quarter of 1996.

"National account statistics are not yet available, but preliminary estimates indicate that, on a seasonally adjusted and annualised basis, the current account deficit declined by approximately six billion rand to about 10 billion rand," Stals said in a statement.
The revised estimate for the annualised second quarter deficit was 16 billion.
Stals said the South African economy was now moving into a period of consolidation after three years of increasing growth rates, which should help the rand stabilise.

"During this consolidation period rates of growth in some of the more important macro-economic aggregates such as gross domestic expenditure will decline to lower, but more sustainable levels," he said.

The governor added that he believed the consolidation of the economy provided an opportunity to restore the equilibrium in South Africa's overall balance of payments "which should support a more stable exchange rate for the rand".
At the same time, it opened a window of opportunity for a necessary reduction in the rates of increase in bank credit extension and money supply growth.
Stals, who said he was hiking the key Bank rate to 17 percent from 16 percent from November 21, said firm action was needed now to keep the economy on track.
"Unless this opportunity is grasped South Africa will have to face the tribulation of lower economic growth with higher inflation," Stals said.
He added that this would threaten the goals of South Africa's macro-economic plan, announced earlier this year.
The plan is aimed at securing prosperous and stable growth into the next century by doubling annual growth to six percent, creating 400,00 new jobs a year by 2000.
